paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Majority voting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how majority voting accuracy changes as the number of completions \(k\) increases, with four overlaid line series. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (\(k\))” and is shown on a logarithmic (base-2) scale with tick labels at \(2^0, 2^1, 2^2, \ldots, 2^8\) (regularly spaced by one exponent). The y-axis is labeled “Majority voting accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from about 0.25 up to about 0.62, with labeled ticks at approximately 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6. A dark blue solid line with circular markers starts near 0.43 at \(2^0\), stays near 0.43 at \(2^1\), then rises through about 0.49 (\(2^2\)), 0.53 (\(2^3\)), 0.57 (\(2^4\)), reaching around 0.60 by \(2^6\) and ending near 0.61–0.62 at \(2^8\). A green solid line with triangular markers closely tracks the dark blue series, beginning around 0.43 at \(2^0\)–\(2^1\), increasing to roughly 0.49 at \(2^2\), around 0.54 at \(2^3\), and ending near 0.61–0.62 at \(2^8\). A light blue solid line with circular markers begins around 0.25 at \(2^0\) and \(2^1\), increases to about 0.30 at \(2^2\), about 0.36 at \(2^3\), about 0.39 at \(2^4\), and rises gradually to roughly 0.43–0.44 by \(2^8\). A light green solid line with triangular markers follows a similar trajectory to the light blue series, starting near 0.25 at \(2^0\)–\(2^1\), reaching about 0.30 at \(2^2\), about 0.36 at \(2^3\), and ending around 0.44 at \(2^8\).
